clips.text_zh: BTC定黃金？十年長揸揀邊樣好。有人話BTC係digital gold，又有人話黃金先係真正嘅store of value。我啱啱喺prop firm燒咗一注學費，睇到呢個帖又想all-in。唔好再嘈喇🙏
clips.text_en_b1: Bitcoin vs Gold. If you had to hold only one for the next 10 years, would you choose Bitcoin or gold? What makes your choice better than the other? Most Bitcoin supporters online call it digital gold and say the supply is fixed at 21 million coins.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ thread asking which asset to hold for the next decade

signal.rationale: OP asks a comparison question, no clear entry setup

clips.text_en_b2: Bitcoin or gold: if you could hold only one for the next ten years, which would you choose, and what makes it superior? Most Bitcoin supporters describe it as “digital gold,” largely because its supply is capped at 21 million coins. Gold supporters, however, regard it as the more reliable store of value. I have already paid a painful tuition fee at a prop firm, so I would genuinely appreciate a straight answer before doing anything reckless.
clips.text_en_c1: Forced to choose between Bitcoin and gold as a ten-year hold, which would genuinely prevail? Bitcoin advocates routinely brandish the 'digital gold' narrative, pointing to its hard-capped supply of twenty-one million coins, whereas traditionalists counter that bullion has weathered centuries of monetary upheaval precisely because it possesses no counterparty risk. Having just haemorrhaged capital on a proprietary prop firm trial, I find myself eyeing this thread with dangerous conviction. Could anyone actually settle this debate once and for all, rather than recycling the same partisan talking points ad infinitum?
clips.text_en_c2: The perennial question resurfaces: if one were compelled to hold a single asset for the coming decade, would Bitcoin or gold prove the superior store of value? Advocates of the former brandish the term digital gold, pointing to its hard-capped supply of twenty-one million coins as a deterministic bulwark against monetary debasement, whereas traditionalists counter that millennia of human consensus render bullion uniquely resistant to regulatory whim and technological obsolescence. Both arguments carry genuine weight, yet each rests on assumptions about liquidity, custodial risk, and macro tail-events that rarely receive adequate scrutiny. The decision, ultimately, hinges less on ideological conviction than on one's appetite for volatility versus the quiet erosion of purchasing power that gold's proponents are so fond of invoking.

clips.text_zh: 係咪時候入TSLA？CyberCab、SpaceX合併、Optimus——全部都未priced in。我份糧就嚟燒晒喺CFD度，睇完又想加倉。Elon你唔好再玩我🙏
clips.text_en_b1: Is it a good time to buy Tesla? It seems like it will at least double from here considering CyberCabs, SpaceX merger potential, and Optimus. The market is still underpricing all three of those catalysts right now.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ thread arguing TSLA is a double from current levels

signal.rationale: OP explicitly argues TSLA doubles from here on Cybercab, SpaceX merger and Optimus catalysts

clips.text_en_b2: Is it finally a good time to buy Tesla, or am I setting myself up for another round of expensive lessons? The bull case appears to rest on three potential catalysts: CyberCabs, a possible SpaceX merger, and Optimus. Although each project remains surrounded by uncertainty, all three seem substantially underpriced by the market. My salary is already being eaten alive by leveraged CFD losses, yet seeing these claims still makes me want to add more exposure. Elon, please stop playing with my financial well-being.
clips.text_en_c1: Is Tesla genuinely undervalued at present levels, given the constellation of catalysts that mainstream analysts appear to be dismissing? CyberCab's autonomous rollout, the prospective SpaceX merger that would unlock latent shareholder value, and Optimus's commercial trajectory collectively suggest that a doubling from here hardly constitutes an unreasonable expectation. The market, it seems, is still failing to price in any of these tailwinds properly. Having already torched a considerable portion of my salary on leveraged CFD positions, I am nevertheless contemplating whether to increase my exposure, despite the obvious risks.
clips.text_en_c2: Is Tesla genuinely attractive at current valuations, or merely a Rorschach test upon which the bullish project whatever narrative suits them? Proponents contend that the equity remains substantially undervalued once one accounts for the optionality embedded in CyberCab's autonomous ambitions, the latent upside from any SpaceX-related corporate restructuring, and the longer-horizon thesis surrounding Optimus and humanoid robotics. Skeptics, reasonably, counter that none of these catalysts have yet generated material revenue and that the market's reluctance to price them reflects not myopia but appropriate skepticism. The gap between these positions is unlikely to narrow absent a concrete earnings inflection. Until then, anyone contemplating fresh exposure might consider whether doubling from here constitutes prudent asymmetric upside or simply the gravitational pull of a story one desperately wishes to believe. Your CFD position, presumably, awaits a verdict.

clips.text_zh: Nitter又返嚟啦。X又嚟搞cease and desist，連embed都告。搞咁多最後都係逼到啲人自建instance。同AI搶飯碗一樣，點閂都閂唔晒🧐
clips.text_en_b1: Nitter is back online. X Corp saw a FOSS front-end letting people use X without ads or tracking, then sent a cease and desist letter to the project under the Texas Harmful Access by Computer Act and Lanham Act. They even hit unrelated embed sites like TwitterWebViewer.
clips.source_hint: /g/ thread on X Corp suing Nitter and alt front-ends

signal.rationale: Tech news observation, not a trade setup

clips.text_en_b2: Nitter is back online, although X has reportedly gone after it with another cease-and-desist demand. What makes this particularly frustrating is the legal basis: X targeted a free, open-source front end that allowed users to browse without advertisements or tracking, citing the Texas Harmful Access by Computer Act and the Lanham Act. It even pursued unrelated embedding services such as TwitterWebViewer. Although these tactics may shut down individual projects, they also push people towards self-hosted instances, where they are far harder to remove.
clips.text_en_c1: Nitter has resurfaced, much to the relief of anyone who values frictionless access to public discourse without surrendering their data to surveillance capitalism. X Corp, evidently unwilling to tolerate even this modest encroachment upon its advertising hegemony, has resorted to issuing cease and desist correspondence, citing the Texas Harmful Access by Computer Act alongside the Lanham Act. Curiously, they have also targeted peripheral embed services such as TwitterWebViewer, which had absolutely nothing to do with the underlying dispute. It resembles AI displacing workers: however aggressively the gates are slammed shut, determined individuals will inevitably construct their own ingress.
clips.text_en_c2: Nitter, the venerable FOSS front-end that long allowed users to peruse X without surrendering their attention to algorithmic feeds or invasive tracking, has resurfaced after yet another legal offensive from Elon Musk's legal apparatus. This time the cease and desist invokes both the Texas Harmful Access by Computer Act and the Lanham Act, signalling a noticeably aggressive posture that extends even to peripheral services such as TwitterWebViewer, whose only offence appears to have been rendering embedded posts. The episode illustrates, once more, how institutional pressure tends to atomise rather than extinguish open-source communities; forks proliferate, instances multiply across jurisdictions less solicitous of American IP maximalism, and the underlying demand persists regardless of how vigorously the upstream platform litigates. Whack-a-mole, in other words, has become the structural condition of contemporary digital life.

clips.text_zh: 點解美國肥佬特別多？歐洲同東亞都工業化、都唔缺糧，點解就係美國肥到咁？我返到HK覺得呢度細但至少行得出去，美國大但坐喺度🧐
clips.text_en_b1: Why does America uniquely suffer from such a rampant obesity problem? Europe and East Asia are also heavily industrialized countries with abundant local food. What exactly is America doing differently that is leading to such an obese population today?
clips.source_hint: /pol/ thread asking why America is more obese than Europe or East Asia
clips.text_en_b2: Why does the United States appear to have a uniquely severe obesity problem? Europe and East Asia are highly industrialized too, and none of these regions suffers from a serious shortage of food, so industrial development and food availability cannot fully explain the difference. Something about American living conditions is clearly having a powerful effect. After returning to Hong Kong, I was struck by the contrast: the city is cramped, but it forces you to walk, whereas the US is spacious and seems designed for…
clips.text_en_c1: Why does the United States, alone among heavily industrialised nations, exhibit such a disproportionate obesity epidemic? Europe and East Asia have undergone comparable economic development, possess equally abundant food supplies, and yet demonstrate markedly lower rates of metabolic dysfunction. Whatever distinguishing factor is at play, whether cultural, infrastructural, or regulatory, it clearly transcends mere caloric availability. Returning to Hong Kong after an extended stay abroad, I am struck by how compact the city feels, yet one can actually traverse it on foot; America sprawls endlessly, but its inhabitants remain, paradoxically, sedentary.
clips.text_en_c2: Why does the United States manifest such a singularly acute obesity epidemic when comparable industrialised societies, from Western Europe through Japan and Korea, enjoy broadly equivalent caloric abundance without comparable metabolic consequence? The anomaly resists any monocausal explanation, though several contributing vectors are reasonably well documented: sprawling suburban morphology that renders car dependency effectively mandatory, aggressive subsidisation of high-fructose corn syrup and ultra-processed foods, the collapse of routine physical activity accompanying sedentary service-sector employment, and a healthcare system that treats the downstream pathologies of obesity rather than their upstream determinants. Cultural normalisation of portion sizes and the relentless marketing engineered toward children further compound matters.

clips.text_zh: 男主角你prefer Wolverine嗰種粗獷毛人，定Link嗰種smooth一啲？我打到S15排位緊，講真角色造型真係影響我想唔想買隻game lol
clips.text_en_b1: Do you prefer if game developers designed more hairy, rugged male protagonists like Wolverine, or more smooth, feminine male protagonists like Link? The aesthetic choice shapes the whole vibe of the game.
clips.source_hint: /v/ thread on male protagonist design preferences
clips.text_en_b2: Which kind of male protagonist do you prefer: the hairy, rugged archetype represented by Wolverine, or the smoother, more feminine-looking hero embodied by Link? This is not merely a cosmetic detail, because character design shapes the atmosphere, tone, and emotional identity of an entire game. I have been grinding my way through Season 15 ranked matches lately, but the protagonist’s appearance can still determine whether a game feels worth buying. A strong visual identity may matter more than developers are willing to admit.
clips.text_en_c1: When developers conceptualise a male protagonist, which aesthetic archetype resonates more strongly with contemporary audiences: the rugged, hyper-masculine sensibility epitomised by Wolverine, or the smoother, almost androgynous presentation exemplified by Link? This is hardly a trivial consideration, since the protagonist's visual identity functions as the primary conduit through which players forge an emotional attachment to the entire experience. As I grind through Season 15 ranked matches, I find myself reflecting that character design frequently determines whether I purchase a title at all, an admittedly superficial but undeniably powerful heuristic.
clips.text_en_c2: Consider, for a moment, the philosophical question of protagonist design: should the contemporary action-adventure lead embody the rugged, hirsute archetype epitomised by Wolverine, bristling with feral masculinity and scarred by an implied history of violence, or ought designers instead favour the smoother, more androgynous aesthetic exemplified by Link, whose grace and ambiguity permit broader player projection? Neither extreme, of course, exists in isolation; the medium has cycled through these ideals for decades, and the current pendulum swing toward latter-day pretty boys reflects commercial calculation as much as artistic preference. Aesthetic decisions of this kind, however ostensibly superficial, exert an outsized gravitational pull on purchase intent, since players frequently confess, half sheepishly, that visual identification with a protagonist matters more than mechanical depth.

clips.text_zh: 18%體脂，日行15K-20K步，cut 500kcal，加埋walking 1000kcal赤字，4星期啦體重完全唔郁。我同肥仔信傾完佢笑我，連deadlift都仲未破2pl8🧐
clips.text_en_b1: Sup guys, 18% body fat here. Walking 15k to 20k steps a day and burning 500 to 800 calories from walking, plus a 500 calorie food cut, total 1000 kcal deficit. Progressive overload is still working, but the scale has not moved in 4 weeks.
clips.source_hint: /fit/ thread on a guy stuck at 18% body fat despite a 1000 kcal deficit
clips.text_en_b2: Guys, I need some straight advice because I am stuck at roughly 18 percent body fat, and the scale has not moved for four weeks. I walk between 15,000 and 20,000 steps every day, while tracking suggests that I burn around 500 to 800 calories from walking alone. On top of that, I cut roughly 500 calories from my diet, producing a daily deficit of about 1,000 kcal.
clips.text_en_c1: Fellow lifters, I find myself in a rather perplexing predicament: presently sitting at approximately eighteen percent body fat, I have been accumulating between fifteen and twenty thousand steps daily, expending anywhere from five to eight hundred calories through ambulatory activity alone, whilst simultaneously maintaining a five-hundred-kilocalorie dietary deficit, yielding a combined shortfall of roughly one thousand calories. Progressive overload on my compound lifts continues to function admirably, yet the scale has remained stubbornly indifferent over four consecutive weeks. After confiding in a friend, he simply laughed at my frustration.
clips.text_en_c2: A familiar lament resounds across the lifting forums: eighteen percent body fat, faithfully accumulating between fifteen and twenty thousand daily steps, sustaining a five-hundred-calorie dietary deficit augmented by roughly a thousand additional kilocalories expended through low-intensity ambulation, yet the scale has obstinately refused to register movement across four consecutive weeks. The iron itself tells a more encouraging tale, as progressive overload continues to deliver incremental strength gains and the deadlift edges ever closer, though not quite past, the cherished two-plate milestone. The dissonance is instructive: adipose redistribution, water retention accompanying muscular adaptation, and the body's homeostatic resistance to sustained caloric restriction collectively conspire to render weekly weigh-ins a singularly unreliable metric. Patience, recalibrated expectations, and perhaps a body-composition measurement rather than a bathroom scale would collectively prove more diagnostic than continued frustration.

clips.text_zh: 夏天就嚟完喇，新番揀咗未？我自己S15打到天昏地暗都仲抽到時間睇番，Gundam 00嗰陣嘅熱血返晒嚟。今季有乜嘢值得追？🙏
clips.text_en_b1: Summer is ending. Have you decided on your anime of the season yet? With so many shows dropping at once, picking what to actually watch is harder than ever. Drop your top pick and tell us why.
clips.source_hint: /a/ thread asking anons to pick their anime of the season
clips.text_en_b2: Summer is nearly over, so have you finally chosen your anime of the season? New shows are arriving in such a constant stream that finding the time to watch them properly has become almost as difficult as keeping up with ranked games. Somehow, despite spending what feels like every waking hour grinding through Season 15, I have still managed to squeeze in a few episodes. In fact, watching Gundam 00 again brought back the same热血 and sense of excitement I felt years ago.
clips.text_en_c1: With summer drawing to a close, the perennial question resurfaces: which series deserves the coveted 'anime of the season' designation? The sheer volume of simulcast offerings this season has made curation genuinely formidable, particularly for viewers juggling demanding schedules. Despite grinding through Season 15 ranked matches until the small hours, I have somehow managed to carve out sufficient bandwidth to keep abreast of the new releases, and that nostalgic Mobile Suit Gundam 00 fervour has resurfaced with full intensity. What hidden gems merit attention?
clips.text_en_c2: Summer's waning days compel the perennial ritual of seasonal curation, and the autumn slate appears, at first inspection, unusually crowded with competing claims upon one's diminishing leisure hours. The miracle, surely, lies in squeezing any anime between ranked sessions that themselves stretch past midnight, yet the habit endures because certain shows reanimate something one had rather forgotten existed: the uncomplicated ardour of a properly executed Gundam 00-era mech opera, say, or the quieter pleasures of a contemplative drama that asks nothing of the viewer beyond sustained attention. This season offers the usual surfeit of isekai derivative works, a handful of adaptations whose faithfulness to source material remains contested, and perhaps one or two genuine surprises awaiting discovery.
